posts.title: Geely Auto lifts export goal to 920,000 as overseas becomes only growth engine
posts.summary:
The new target represents nearly 120% growth from 2025 exports, with the company targeting a combined 1,000,000-vehicle scale across 5 key overseas markets.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: Geely Auto has aggressively raised its 2026 export target to 920,000 vehicles, a 44% increase from its original goal and a 120% jump over 2025 levels.
The company is pivoting heavily toward international markets as a primary growth engine, following a 22.6% decline in domestic China sales during the first half of the year.
New energy vehicles (NEVs) are the primary driver of this international expansion, accounting for 59% of total exports in July with a 616% year-on-year growth rate.
Geely has identified five key geographic regions, including ASEAN and Pan-Europe, to support a long-term goal of reaching a 1,000,000-vehicle scale in overseas markets.

posts.title: CATL says core operations carbon neutral by end-2025, supply chain next
posts.summary:
CATL said its supply chain accounts for more than 80% of its products' carbon emissions, and it aims to achieve value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035.
For details, please visit CnEVPost (cnev.co).
bullets: CATL has officially achieved carbon neutrality across its core operations by the end of 2025, utilizing 100% zero-carbon electricity across its manufacturing facilities.
The company has set a new, more ambitious target to achieve full value-chain carbon neutrality by 2035, addressing the supply chain which accounts for over 80% of its product lifecycle emissions.
To manage this transition, CATL has implemented a proprietary Carbon Chain Management System (CCMS) to track real-world carbon data from mineral extraction through component manufacturing.
Despite scaling production to 748 GWh in 2025, CATL reported a 77% reduction in carbon-emissions intensity over the last two years, signaling a decoupling of manufacturing growth from carbon output.

posts.title: Stripe Acquiring OpenRouter, Aggregating AI?, Flipping the Business Model
posts.summary: Stripe is reportedly acquiring OpenRouter, an implicit bet on a future market of models and the chance at Aggregation.
bullets: Stripe's reported acquisition of OpenRouter signals a strategic pivot toward becoming a central aggregator in the fragmented AI model landscape.
By controlling the infrastructure layer for model access, Stripe aims to capture value from the proliferation of AI services rather than just processing payments.
This move represents a fundamental shift in Stripe's business model, moving from a pure-play financial services provider to a critical middleware layer for the AI ecosystem.
The acquisition positions Stripe to benefit from the 'Aggregation Theory' by commoditizing individual model providers while becoming the indispensable gateway for developers.

posts.title: 800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid To Gate
posts.summary:
The next power bottleneck is no longer just inside the accelerator — it is the full conversion path from medium-voltage AC to sub-1V silicon.
The post 800VDC Pushes AI Power Design From Grid To Gate appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: AI data center power requirements are scaling rapidly, with server rack demands projected to increase from 125 kilowatts today to 1 megawatt in the near future.
To manage these loads, hyperscalers are transitioning from traditional 48V or 12V architectures to 800VDC systems to improve efficiency and reduce conversion losses.

The shift necessitates a redesign of the entire power delivery chain, moving away from multi-stage conversion toward solid-state transformers that bridge the gap between medium-voltage grids and sub-1V silicon.
Minimizing thermal loss during the conversion from high-voltage AC to low-voltage DC is now a critical factor for maintaining the performance and reliability of high-density AI accelerators.

posts.title: The Download: dead robot friends and the “censorship-industrial complex”
posts.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. What happens when a kid’s robot best friend dies? When Xander first met Moxie, she taught him how to calm down when he was anxious or mad. Six years later, she…
bullets: The collapse of AI companion robot manufacturers, such as the maker of the Moxie device, highlights significant consumer risks regarding product longevity and the reliance on centralized cloud servers for hardware functionality.

The 'censorship-industrial complex' theory has transitioned from fringe political discourse into active US policy, potentially reshaping how government agencies and Big Tech platforms collaborate on content moderation.
The US government is intensifying efforts to force international allies to choose sides in the global AI race, specifically pressuring partners to avoid China’s rival AI initiatives.

Beijing is increasingly leveraging open-weight AI models to expand its governance capabilities, creating a strategic divide within the White House regarding the risks and benefits of open-source AI development.
